methods.label: Express both quantities in terms of P
methods.explanation:
Expressing both \(M\) and \(N\) as fractions of \(P\) lets us compare them directly. The given percentages give
\[
Q=\frac15P,\qquad M=\frac3{10}Q=\frac3{50}P,\qquad N=\frac12P.
\]
The ratio \(M/N\) requires \(N\ne0\), so \(P\ne0\). We may therefore cancel the common factor \(P\):
\[
\frac{M}{N}=\frac{3/50}{1/2}=\frac3{50}\cdot2=\frac3{25}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac3{25}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
